implementation_notes: __init__ cannot return a failure value, so the idiomatic factory is a @classmethod alternate constructor with a domain name (Order.from_cart, Subscription.register) that validates with guard clauses and then calls cls(...); frozen dataclasses put the invariants in __post_init__, and dataclasses.replace()/object.__new__ stay documented bypasses the factory cannot close. What replaces the classic factory class is the named classmethod (or a module-level function); a standalone factory object is justified when creation must load aggregates through repository ports or translate an external payload, where pydantic-style model_validate is the library alternative.
pitfalls: dataclasses.replace() and object.__new__ build instances without calling __post_init__ or the classmethod, so 'always valid' is a convention until the class stops exposing a usable constructor.
Validation that needs I/O or other aggregates cannot live in __post_init__ without making the model impossible to build offline; put it in a standalone factory that holds the ports.
Subclasses that override __post_init__ or the generated __init__ can silently drop a check; keep the rules in one place and exercise the subclass paths in tests.
